q: How much can a discom charge for standby power under green energy open access?
title: Standby charges on green open access
short: Standby charges under green energy open access are capped at 25% of the energy charges of your tariff category, after the January 2023 amendment raised the cap from 10%. They do not apply at all if you give the discom notice before the day ahead market closes on the day before delivery.
audience: Green open access consumers whose generator or line may be unavailable

p: Standby power is what the discom supplies when your open access source fails, for example a generator outage or a transmission fault. The Rules say the charge should reflect the discom's cost of keeping that support ready.

ul: Cap: not more than 25% of the energy charges applicable to your consumer tariff category (G.S.R. 59(E), 27 January 2023). The original 2022 Rules set 10%.
Exemption: no standby charge if you notify the discom at least a day ahead, before the closure time of the Day Ahead Market on the day before delivery.
Your state commission specifies the actual charge within that cap.

p: Build the standby charge into your landed cost comparison only for the outage days you expect, and agree with your developer how they will warn you of planned maintenance early enough to give notice and avoid it.

example.title: Worked example: the cap in rupees (illustrative rates)
lines: Energy charge for your HT industrial category: ₹7.00 per kWh
Maximum standby charge: 25% x 7.00 = ₹1.75 per kWh, on top of the energy charge for those units
With day ahead notice given in time: no standby charge
example.note: The rate is assumed; your state commission sets the actual charge.

senseible: Senseible keeps standby units on the bill as discom units, so they appear in location-based Scope 2 on the grid factor rather than being counted as green.
